steps.reasoning:
We have a big requirement:

1. Find local authorities (Wales) that did NOT see an overall decrease in number of households since 2011 (so households increased or stayed same). According to source: In Wales, only three local authorities had decreases: Gwynedd (2.6% decrease), Ceredigion (2.1% decrease), Blaenau Gwent (0.4% decrease). Thus all others had increase.

So list of all local authorities (22 total) minus those three: that is 19 local authorities had no decrease.

2. Out of these, identify those with population <120,000 at mid-year 2021 and not in North Wales region.

We need population data mid-2021 for each local authority.

From earlier sources: mid-2021? The 2021 census population? We see a table: Cardiff 362,308; Swansea 238,490; Rhondda Cynon Taf 237,651; Carmarthenshire 187,897; Caerphilly 175,952; Newport 159,592; Flintshire 154,962; Bridgend 145,488; Neath Port Talbot 142,289; Wrexham 135,117; Powys 133,169; Vale of Glamorgan 131,939; Pembrokeshire 123,360; Gwynedd 117,393 (but it's one of the decreasing households); Conwy 114,741; Denbighshire 95,817; Monmouthshire 92,957; Torfaen 92,276; Ceredigion 71,475 (decrease households), Isle of Anglesey 68,878; Blaenau Gwent 66,904; Merthyr Tydfil 58,836.

Thus population <120,000 includes: Gwynedd (but households decreased, so exclude), Conwy, Denbighshire, Monmouthshire, Torfaen, Ceredigion (exclude due to households decreased), Isle of Anglesey, Blaenau Gwent, Merthyr Tydfil. These nine local authorities. But we need those not in North Wales region. North Wales includes: Anglesey, Caerphilly? Wait Caerphilly is mid-Wales; North Wales is the region comprising Anglesey (Isle), Conwy, Denbighshire, Flintshire, Gwynedd, Wrexham? Actually Wrexham is in North Wales too. But we need to exclude any in North Wales region. So we need to know which of the nine are in North Wales: Anglesey (Isle of Anglesey), Conwy, Denbighshire, Flintshire (but its population >120k, not in list), Gwynedd, Wrexham (not in list). So the nine: Gwynedd, Conwy, Denbighshire, Monmouthshire, Torfaen, Ceredigion, Isle of Anglesey, Blaenau Gwent, Merthyr Tydfil.

Exclude North Wales: remove Gwynedd, Conwy, Denbighshire, Isle of Anglesey, Wrexham (not included), probably.

Thus remaining: Monmouthshire, Torfaen, Ceredigion (but households decreased, so exclude), Blaenau Gwent, Merthyr Tydfil. Keep only those that had no decrease households: That excludes Ceredigion. So candidate local authorities: Monmouthshire, Torfaen, Blaenau Gwent, Merthyr Tydfil. Also check if Merthyr Tydfil has populations <120k? Yes 58,836. Merthyr Tydfil population <120k, households not decreased (yes Merthyr population but households? Household in Merthyr not decreased per earlier list; households decreased only in Gwynedd, Ceredigion, Blaenau Gwent. Wait earlier list said households decreased: Gwynedd, Ceredigion, Blaenau Gwent. So Blaenau Gwent had a decrease, so exclude. Actually earlier excerpt: "The areas where there were decreases in the number of households were Gwynedd (2.6% decrease), Ceredigion (2.1% decrease) and Blaenau Gwent (0.4% decrease)." Yes Blaenau Gwent had decrease households, so exclude. So Blaenau Gwent excluded.

Now candidates: Monmouthshire, Torfaen, Merthyr Tydfil. But need to confirm Merthyr had no decrease households: True (households only 3 decreased, Merthyr not listed). So Merthyr Tydfil qualifies.

Thus left: Monmouthshire, Torfaen, Merthyr Tydfil. Check population <120,000: Monmouthshire 92,957; Torfaen 92,276; Merthyr 58,836 – all satisfy.

Now we need to identify which of these have seen an increase of over 2% in people aged 25 to 44 between mid-year 2021 and mid-year 2022.

We need mid-year population estimates for 2021 and 2022 for these local authorities by age group 25-44.

We must find mid-year population estimates for 2021 and 2022; the dataset we can query via Nomis or Stats Wales.

We could use Nomis dataset "population estimates at mid-year 2022" but must extract 25-44 age group.

Alternatively, Stats Wales mid-year estimates 2022 might be there.

Let's search for Monmouthshire age 25 to 44 mid-2021 and mid-2022.

Search query.

## Spotlight
### Population estimates for England and Wales: mid-2025
#### What's in the bulletin?
*   The population of England and Wales continued to grow in the year to mid-2025, reaching an estimated 62.0 million people. The size of the population is estimated to have increased by 224,900 (0.4%) from mid-2024, the lowest rate of increase since mid-2020. This was primarily because of a fall in international net migration, but natural change (births minus deaths) was also slightly lower in the year to mid-2025.  
*   The number of people immigrating to England and Wales from outside the UK decreased in the year to mid-2025, compared with the previous year. The number of people emigrating from England and Wales to outside the UK increased in the same period. ## The population reached nearly 93,000
Between the last two censuses (held in 2011 and 2021), the population of Monmouthshire increased by 1.8%, from around 91,300 in 2011 to around 93,000 in 2021.
This means Monmouthshire's population increased by a greater percentage than the overall population of Wales. The population of Wales increased by 1.4%, from 3,063,000 to 3,107,000.
In 2021, Monmouthshire was home to around 0.8 people per football pitch-sized piece of land. This area was the eighth-least densely populated out of all 22 local authority areas across Wales.
This article generally uses percentages to enable comparisons over time and between areas. The percentage point change is also used to show the difference between the 2011 and 2021 percentages.

## An older Monmouthshire
Between the last two censuses, the average (median) age of Monmouthshire increased by four years, from 45 to 49 years of age.
This area had a higher average (median) age than nearby Torfaen (42 years) and the joint second-highest average (median) age in Wales (alongside Conwy and behind Powys).
The median age is the age of the person in the middle of the group, meaning that one half of the group is younger than that person and the other half is older.
The number of people aged 65 to 74 years rose by around 2,500 (an increase of 25.1%), while the number of residents between 35 and 49 years fell by just under 3,800 (19.4% decrease).

## Fall in proportion of Welsh speakers
The percentage of Welsh speakers in Monmouthshire fell from 9.9% in 2011 to 8.7% in 2021.
In 2021, there were around 950 fewer Welsh-speaking Monmouthshire residents (over the age of three years) compared with 2011. The number of people who did not speak Welsh increased by 3,000.
In nearby Torfaen, 8.2% of people over the age of three years could speak Welsh, down from 9.8% at the 2011 Census. Across Wales, the percentage of Welsh speakers fell from 19.0% to 17.8%.
Cardiff was one of the few areas that saw an increase in the percentage of Welsh speakers (from 11.1% in 2011 to 12.2% in 2021), while Carmarthenshire saw the largest fall (from 43.9% to 39.9%).

## Fall in proportion of Welsh speakers
The percentage of Welsh speakers in Monmouthshire fell from 9.9% in 2011 to 8.7% in 2021.
In 2021, there were around 950 fewer Welsh-speaking Monmouthshire residents (over the age of three years) compared with 2011. The number of people who did not speak Welsh increased by 3,000.
In nearby Torfaen, 8.2% of people over the age of three years could speak Welsh, down from 9.8% at the 2011 Census. Across Wales, the percentage of Welsh speakers fell from 19.0% to 17.8%.
Cardiff was one of the few areas that saw an increase in the percentage of Welsh speakers (from 11.1% in 2011 to 12.2% in 2021), while Carmarthenshire saw the largest fall (from 43.9% to 39.9%).

#### What's in the bulletin?
*   The population of the UK continued to grow in the year to mid-2025, reaching an estimated 69.5 million people. The size of the population is estimated to have increased by 228,000 (0.3%) from mid-2024, the lowest rate of increase since mid-2020.  
*   There was an increase in population for England of 0.4%, with Scotland and Northern Ireland having very small population growth (less than 0.1%). Wales had a small decrease in population (negative 0.1%).  
*   The changes in population for Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland to mid-2025 are small. ## Spotlight
### Population estimates for England and Wales: mid-2025
#### What's in the bulletin?
*   The population of England and Wales continued to grow in the year to mid-2025, reaching an estimated 62.0 million people. The size of the population is estimated to have increased by 224,900 (0.4%) from mid-2024, the lowest rate of increase since mid-2020. This was primarily because of a fall in international net migration, but natural change (births minus deaths) was also slightly lower in the year to mid-2025.  
*   The number of people immigrating to England and Wales from outside the UK decreased in the year to mid-2025, compared with the previous year. The number of people emigrating from England and Wales to outside the UK increased in the same period. This led to an overall decrease in net international migration compared with the previous year.  
*   There was a decrease in the number of births and deaths in the year to mid-2025, compared with the previous year.

## Overview
Summary of dataset and variables  
This dataset provides population estimates for the local authorities in Wales, the English regions and the UK countries for the period from 1991 onwards by sex and single year of age.
It should be noted that for mid-2020 there are some definitional changes, particularly affecting the migration components, compared with mid-2019 population estimates data and it is advised users read the Quality and Methodology Information section on the Office for National Statistics website.
For Wales, England and Northern Ireland, the mid-2021 population estimates are the first population estimates to be based on the 2021 censuses for these countries. For Scotland, the census was moved to 2022. The mid-2022 population estimates are the first population estimates to be based on the 2022 Census for Scotland.
On 23 November 2023, the data set from 2012 to 2020 for Wales and England were rebased to be consistent with the results of Census 2021. Northern Ireland published rebased 2012 to 2020 data on 29 June 2023. Scotland published rebased 2012 to 2020 data on 9 July 2024.
On 29 July 2026 estimates for mid-2022, mid-2023 and mid-2024 were revised by the ONS to account for updated estimates of international migration for Wales and England.
Internal migration estimates for mid-2023 have been produced using a different method to previous years, following a change to the variables available in the Higher Education Statistics Agency data.
Data collection or calculation  
The Office for National Statistics (ONS) publish mid-year population estimates for Wales and England as a whole. Further information on how the data are calculated can be found on the ONS' website. A link can be found in the weblink section.
Statistical quality  
The Office for National Statistics (ONS) publish mid-year population estimates for Wales and England as a whole. Further information on statistical quality can be found on the ONS' website. A link can be found in the weblink section.
